sentences.text:
---- A
 versus
 1 - State Of Chhattisgarh Through Police Station Kondagaon, District
 Kondagaon, C.G.
 ---- Resp
For Applicant : Mr. Manoj Paranjpe, Advocate For Respondent : Mr. Rajeev Bharat, Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 12/11/2024
1.

Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No. 295 of 2023, registered at Police Station - Kondagaon, District - Kondagaon (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 471 and 409 of the Indian Penal Code.

The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 27.02.2024 in M.Cr.C. No.337 of 2024.
2.

The case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the applicant, who was posted as Assistant Grade-II in the office of the Assistant Director, Fisheries, District Kondagaon, from 13.05.2022 to 01.05.2023,
misappropriated an amount of 43,74,794 by forging documents and transferred the funds from the government account to his own account.
One more crime is registered against applicant of similar nature in which the allegation of misappropriation of funds is to the tune of Rs.81,84,200/-.

3. Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is not pressing this repeat bail application on merits and is only seeking bail on the ground of delay in trial and the period of pretrial detention of applicant since 02.09.2023.

In support of his contention, he also referred to the documents filed Sanjay Kumar Gadpale vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98301648/
1 along with the bail application.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, applicant may be released on bail.
4. Learned State counsel opposes the submission of learned counsel for applicant and would submit that allegation against applicant is serious in nature.
There are allegation of transfer of government funds by applicant in his own bank accounts by forging documents.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
6. Perusal of the order-sheet would show that the examination-in-chief of prosecution witness has been stopped for want of report of the State Examiner.
As per instructions received by learned State counsel today, it is still awaited.

7. Considering the aforementioned facts of the case, period of pretrial detention of applicant and also considering the fact that applicant being the government servant, there is no likelihood of his absconding, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.

8. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one local surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court below on the conditions that:-
a). Applicant shall appear before the trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
(b). Applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c). If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in the future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.
